gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta is a plain sans with wide tracking and tall small letters. Pramukh Rounded sits tight and compact above it, its strokes gently varying where the body's ribbon lines never budge, which is the whole fun of the pairing.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-montserrat-alt: Montserrat Alternates reads round and chalky, its lowercase climbing toward the capital line and its c gaping like a bent paperclip. Pramukh Rounded crowds its letters close, and that tightness against the sans body is the pair's best trick.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-erode: Commanding yet unhurried, Quilon swells and thins in a slow tide, with generous openings in its tall a, e and s. Erode follows as a classic serif with a tall middle band and short ascenders, so paragraphs run smooth and dignified.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-domine: Quilon opens with a display voice, its strokes ebbing and swelling while its tall a, e and s hold wide counters. And Domine answers underneath as a serif with compact ascenders and a slight pinch where curves meet stems, steady and quiet.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-epunda-slab: Big, bold-faced swagger leads here: Quilon's strokes ebb and flow, with crossbars a touch finer than the main stems. And Epunda Slab settles in below as a serif with a gaping c and tall rounded lowercase, giving the page a grounded floor.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-esteban: Quilon's slow ebb and flow of stroke thickness is its signature, along with wide counters in the tall a, e and s. But Esteban does the quieter work as a text serif, its lowercase oversized beside its capitals and its thin parts barely slimmer than the stems.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-fauna-one: Fauna One reads literary and low in contrast, as a text serif with a tall middle band and a generous opening into the e. Quilon grabs attention with its middling swell of stroke; Fauna One is the one for sustained reading.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-glegoo: Editorial through and through, Quilon moves with a moderate stem-to-hairline ratio and wide-open counters in tall a, e and s. And Glegoo meets it as a classic serif with big counters and curves left unclosed, low in contrast and easy to settle into.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hanuman: Hanuman reads traditional, a serif with a high-waisted lowercase. Its s has wide-set terminals, and its low contrast keeps long paragraphs smooth where Quilon's mild, approachable swell would stand out by comparison.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-headland-one: Tall, stately, a little dramatic: Quilon ebbs and flows through its strokes with large open counters in a, e and s. And Headland One backs it up as a classic serif, its letters set well apart and its round o nearly matching a capital O.
